metadata.title: Rodent single-dose pharmacokinetics with serial blood sampling (IV vs PO, v0.3 in-vivo demo)
metadata.purpose: Determine the plasma pharmacokinetic profile and absolute oral bioavailability of a small-molecule test compound in mice after a single intravenous bolus and a single oral dose, using serial blood sampling from the same animals and LC-MS/MS bioanalysis.
metadata.scope: Small-molecule plasma PK in mouse after one IV bolus and one PO gavage dose, with serial lateral-saphenous-vein sampling (no anesthesia). Demonstrates v0.3 in-vivo constructs (studyDesign, compliance, organism samples, step.repeat, acceptanceCriteria). Out of scope: tissue distribution, metabolite ID, multi-dose/steady-state, and large-molecule PK.
metadata.estimatedTime: 1 dosing day (~4 h sampling window) + LC-MS/MS bioanalysis and NCA (2-3 days)
beforeYouBegin: Record the IACUC approval / protocol number in the study file BEFORE any animal work; this study must not start without it (see compliance.iacuc).
Randomize animals to the IV or PO arm by a documented method and record the allocation before dosing (see studyDesign.randomization).
Compute each animal's dose (from body weight) and its maximum cumulative blood-withdrawal cap (~10% of total blood volume) before sampling (table t3).
Decide and record fasting status for the PO arm; it is not fixed by the methods sources (needsReview).
Prepare formulations so the dose fits within route volume limits: IV <=5 mL/kg, PO <=10 mL/kg (Diehl 2001, src2).
Confirm the LC-MS/MS method (internal standard, extraction, calibration range, QC acceptance) is validated for the analyte before bioanalysis.

samples.description: Animals randomized to the IV bolus arm (n=3); each animal is serially sampled across all timepoints. Sex 'male' per Peng 2009 (src1); strain is a study choice (needsReview).

samples.description: Animals randomized to the oral gavage arm (n=3); each animal is serially sampled across all timepoints.

samples.description: Plasma separated from each blood draw by centrifugation; analyte quantified by LC-MS/MS.

tables.title: Serial blood-sampling schedule (same animal, both arms)
tables.note: Seven serial draws from the same animal via lateral saphenous vein (Peng 2009, src1). Cumulative ~140 uL stays within the ~180 uL (10% total blood volume) cap for a 25 g mouse (table t3). Per-draw 20 uL is chosen to satisfy the welfare cap and the assay's required plasma volume; exact value is analyte/assay-specific (needsReview).

tables.title: Non-compartmental PK parameters to derive (per arm)
rows: Area under the curve to last measurable point (linear-up/log-down trapezoidal)
Terminal rate constant (log-linear regression of terminal points)
tables.note: Derived quantities. Formulas are recorded here and echoed as parameter.formula on step s8. Summaries reported mean +/- SD, n=3 per arm.

tables.title: Welfare blood-withdrawal limits (serial sampling)
rows: <=10% of total blood volume per single draw with ~2-3 week recovery
Keep cumulative single-day withdrawal <=10% total blood volume
tables.note: From Diehl 2001 (src2) and Parasuraman 2010 (src3). For a same-day serial study without fluid replacement, cumulative withdrawal is capped conservatively at 10% of total blood volume; compute each animal's cap from its body weight before drawing.

steps.action: Confirm the IACUC approval is on file, enroll and randomize healthy mice to the IV or PO arm, weigh each animal, and compute its dose and cumulative blood-withdrawal cap.

acceptanceCriteria.classification: Enroll only clinically healthy mice with body weight 20-30 g; exclude sick or out-of-range animals
acceptanceCriteria.description: Enrollment inclusion gate before randomization and dosing.

steps.expectedResult: Documented, IACUC-approved study with per-animal weights, arm allocation, and blood-volume caps recorded.
steps.criticalNotes: Do not proceed without a recorded IACUC approval/protocol number (compliance.iacuc). Compute each animal's cap (~10% total blood volume; table t3) before dosing.
steps.safetyNotes: All in-life work only under the approved animal-ethics protocol.

steps.action: Prepare the IV and PO dosing formulations of the test compound at concentrations that deliver the target dose within each route's volume limit.
steps.expectedResult: Two dose formulations ready and characterized (concentration, appearance/solubility).
steps.criticalNotes: Exact vehicle and fasting status are compound/study-specific and not fixed by the methods sources; record them. Doses (IV 1, PO 10 mg/kg) are explicit design choices, not source values.

steps.action: Administer a single IV bolus of the test compound to the IV arm via a lateral tail vein; record the exact dosing time as t=0.
steps.expectedResult: IV arm dosed; per-animal t=0 timestamp logged.

sourceReferences.excerpt: routes of administration and factors to consider

steps.action: Administer a single oral gavage dose of the test compound to the PO arm; record the exact dosing time as t=0.
steps.expectedResult: PO arm dosed; per-animal t=0 timestamp logged.
steps.criticalNotes: Fasting status for the PO arm is not specified by the methods sources; decide and record it (needsReview).

sourceReferences.excerpt: routes of administration and factors to consider

steps.action: Collect serial whole-blood microsamples from the lateral saphenous vein of each animal at every scheduled post-dose timepoint (no anesthesia), into K2-EDTA tubes.

repeat.untilCondition: all 7 timepoints collected, OR the per-animal cumulative withdrawal reaches the 10% total-blood-volume welfare cap (whichever comes first)
repeat.notes: Serial design: every timepoint is drawn from the SAME animal via lateral saphenous vein puncture, requiring no anesthesia (Peng 2009).

parameters.rawText: ~20 uL per serial draw (kept small so 7 draws stay within the 10% blood-volume cap; exact volume set by assay sensitivity)

acceptanceCriteria.classification: Stop serial sampling if cumulative withdrawal would exceed 10% of the animal's total blood volume
acceptanceCriteria.description: Animal-welfare quality gate governing the serial-sampling loop.

steps.expectedResult: A timed concentration series (0-240 min) of whole-blood samples per animal.
steps.criticalNotes: Lateral-saphenous serial sampling needs no anesthesia (Peng 2009, src1). Keep cumulative withdrawal <=10% total blood volume (Diehl 2001 src2; Parasuraman 2010 src3; table t3). Record the exact clock time of each draw for accurate NCA.
steps.safetyNotes: Use approved restraint and sampling sites; minimize distress; apply gentle hemostasis after each draw.

sourceReferences.excerpt: serial blood sampling methodology using the lateral saphenous vein puncture technique ... without the need for anesthesia

steps.action: Centrifuge each blood sample to separate plasma; transfer plasma to labeled cryovials and store frozen until bioanalysis.

parameters.rawText: ~2000 x g (standard plasma separation; confirm per SOP)
store plasma at -80 degC until analysis

acceptanceCriteria.classification: Reject visibly hemolyzed samples or those below the minimum plasma volume required by the assay

steps.expectedResult: Plasma aliquots stored at -80 degC, ready for bioanalysis.
steps.criticalNotes: Centrifugation settings are standard defaults; confirm against lab SOP and the minimum plasma volume the LC-MS/MS method needs.

steps.action: Quantify the test compound in plasma by LC-MS/MS against a matrix-matched calibration curve with internal standard, using blank plasma for standards and QCs; keep the analyst blinded to arm and timepoint via coded samples.

acceptanceCriteria.classification: Run accepted if QCs are within +/-15% of nominal (+/-20% at the LLOQ) and at least 2/3 QC levels pass (FDA/EMA bioanalytical criteria)

steps.expectedResult: A validated plasma concentration for every sample; concentration-time dataset assembled.
steps.criticalNotes: Internal standard, extraction, chromatography, and calibration range are analyte-specific and must come from the validated method (needsReview).

steps.action: Perform non-compartmental analysis (NCA) on the concentration-time data to derive Cmax, Tmax, AUC0-t, AUC0-inf, lambda_z, t1/2, CL, Vss/Vz, and absolute oral bioavailability F%.

parameters.formula: F% = (AUC0-inf_PO x Dose_IV) / (AUC0-inf_IV x Dose_PO) x 100

parameters.rawText: systemic clearance from the IV arm

steps.expectedResult: Full NCA parameter set per arm plus absolute oral bioavailability, summarized as mean +/- SD (n=3 per arm).
steps.criticalNotes: AUC by linear-up/log-down trapezoidal; lambda_z by log-linear regression of terminal points. Specific NCA software is lab-specific (needsReview).

controls.description: Drug-free matrix for LC-MS/MS calibration standards and QC samples.

controls.name: Predose (t=0) baseline sample
controls.description: Confirms absence of analyte before dosing and gives a per-animal baseline.

controls.name: IV reference arm
controls.description: IV data provide the 100% bioavailability reference for computing absolute F of the PO arm.

controls.name: Bioanalytical QC samples (low/mid/high)
controls.description: Bracket each run to confirm assay accuracy and precision.

expectedOutputs: Plasma concentration-time profiles for the IV and PO arms (mean +/- SD, n=3 per arm).
Non-compartmental PK parameters per arm: Cmax, Tmax, AUC0-t, AUC0-inf, t1/2, CL, Vss/Vz.
Complete regulatory/design record: IACUC number, randomization scheme, per-animal weights, doses, and cumulative blood-volume log.

troubleshooting.cause: Too few late timepoints or concentrations near the LLOQ
troubleshooting.solution: Extend the sampling window or improve assay sensitivity; report AUC0-t if extrapolation exceeds 20%.

troubleshooting.cause: Rough saphenous draw or delayed/insufficient centrifugation
troubleshooting.solution: Gentle collection, prompt processing, verify spin conditions and minimum plasma volume.

troubleshooting.cause: Cumulative blood withdrawal approaches 10% of total blood volume
troubleshooting.solution: Reduce per-draw volume or drop non-critical timepoints (table t3); never exceed the cap.

troubleshooting.cause: Dosing/route error, formulation instability, or assay recovery problem
troubleshooting.solution: Verify dose and route records, formulation concentration, and bioanalytical recovery.

safety: Conduct all animal procedures only under the approved IACUC protocol; record the approval number (compliance.iacuc).
Respect the species blood-volume limit (cumulative <=10% of total blood volume) to avoid hypovolemia during serial sampling (Diehl 2001; Parasuraman 2010).
Handle the test compound and organic bioanalytical solvents (e.g. acetonitrile) per SDS in appropriate containment; dispose per compliance.wasteDisposal.

groups.name: IV bolus arm (reference)
groups.treatment: Single intravenous bolus of test compound, 1 mg/kg, <=5 mL/kg, via lateral tail vein at t=0
groups.description: Reference arm defining 100% bioavailability for absolute F; each animal serially sampled across all timepoints.

groups.name: PO gavage arm
groups.treatment: Single oral gavage of test compound, 10 mg/kg, <=10 mL/kg, at t=0
groups.description: Oral arm; each animal serially sampled across all timepoints.

studyDesign.randomization: Healthy mice block-randomized to the IV or PO arm using a computer-generated random sequence, stratified by body weight; allocation recorded before dosing.
studyDesign.blinding: Samples coded at collection; the LC-MS/MS bioanalyst and the PK analyst are blinded to arm and nominal timepoint until concentrations are finalized.
studyDesign.statisticalPlan: Non-compartmental analysis (NCA): AUC by linear-up/log-down trapezoidal; terminal lambda_z by log-linear regression of terminal points; Cmax/Tmax observed; CL = Dose_IV/AUC0-inf_IV; Vss from CL and MRT; t1/2 = ln(2)/lambda_z. Absolute oral bioavailability F% = (AUC0-inf_PO x Dose_IV)/(AUC0-inf_IV x Dose_PO) x 100. Reported as mean +/- SD, n=3 per arm.
studyDesign.notes: Serial (not discrete/composite) sampling: each animal contributes a full concentration-time curve, improving data quality and reducing animal use (Peng 2009). n=3 per arm is a typical first-tier discovery PK choice; set final group size by the study's power/precision needs (needsReview).

compliance.iacuc: All in-life procedures must be reviewed and approved by the Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (IACUC) before any animal work begins. The institution-specific approval/protocol number is assigned per study and must be recorded in the study file before dosing; it is not fabricated here.
compliance.consent: Not applicable - non-human vertebrate study (no human-subjects consent required).
compliance.wasteDisposal: Animal carcasses and blood/plasma disposed as regulated animal/biological waste; needles and lancets to sharps containers; residual test compound and organic bioanalytical solvents (e.g. acetonitrile) collected as chemical hazardous waste. Follow institutional EHS/biosafety and IACUC waste procedures.
compliance.notes: Serial-sampling design implements the 3Rs Reduction principle (same animals sampled across all timepoints), per Peng 2009 (src1); welfare blood-volume limits per Diehl 2001 (src2) and Parasuraman 2010 (src3).

limitations: Plasma PK only; no tissue distribution, metabolite identification, protein-binding correction, or multi-dose/steady-state. Exact vehicle, fasting status, per-draw blood volume, bioanalytical method (internal standard/extraction/chromatography), centrifugation settings, and NCA software are compound/lab-specific and marked needsReview. biosafetyLevel is 'not specified' because hazard depends on the test article; the ethics gate now lives in compliance (IACUC), not in biosafetyLevel as the earlier v0.2 workaround did.
